scope: Account-private manual media annotation foundation; not automatic classification
implemented: Additive SQLite 121 and PostgreSQL 023 migrations store authenticated-owner source references, revisions, SHA-256-shaped fingerprints and ordinary/sexual/disturbing/both labels. No media bytes or message plaintext are accepted.

GET/PUT/DELETE /api/users/me/media-label enforce non-bot authentication, strict bounded JSON, source read or conversation membership checks and current message revision for reads/writes. Removal of one's own annotation remains possible after losing source access.
Storage isolates owners, caps records at 5000 per account, permits existing-key updates and rejects deleted-owner writes. PostgreSQL serializes quota checks on the owner row.
Account anonymization and hard deletion remove owned annotations; personal data export includes only the requesting owner's annotation metadata. No annotation broadcasts are sent to other users.

Client API selects only reference fields and supports request cancellation/current-session guards. Policy helper treats explicit manual labels separately from unknown/error states; it does not claim AI analysis.

Channel/DM attachment groups, visual group attachments and link previews expose private manual labels with load, save, removal and retry controls. Media identity is hashed locally; URLs and plaintext are not included in the reference payload.

UI validates returned source/revision/fingerprint and label enum before applying a persisted choice. Owner, device, source and revision changes replace the annotation component; aborted or old-account/generation responses cannot apply. Writes commit visibility only after server success; errors revert to unknown-media preferences and revoke prior temporary reveals. Annotation mutations close detached media viewers.
